## Summary

The IEEE registry lists three MA-L blocks to "Panasonic Automotive Systems Company of America" at 776 Highway 74 South, Peachtree City, Georgia [1]. A 2013 QNX release describes the company as based in Peachtree City with a Detroit-area operation in Farmington Hills, Michigan, as a division of Panasonic Corporation of North America of Secaucus, New Jersey, and as building infotainment systems for automakers in North America, Europe and Japan on the QNX CAR platform [2]. Panasonic Holdings later moved its automotive systems business into a new parent in which Apollo-managed funds hold 80 percent and Panasonic 20 percent (December 2024); whether that covers this US division is not stated by the source [4].

A MAC in these blocks is most likely a car's head unit or connected-car module [1][2]. TechInsights' teardown of the Panasonic-developed Toyota Tundra head unit 86100-0C381 found Bluetooth 5.1 and dual-band Wi-Fi 6 on 2.4 and 5 GHz from an NXP Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip, a Panasonic AM/FM radio chip and Samsung memory; that this unit carries this division's MAC blocks is inferred, not stated [3]. The FCC grantee code ACJ is listed for Panasonic Corporation of North America, the division's parent, not for the division itself [5].

Founding year, randomization and security history are not documented by the sources consulted; the FCC ID databases refused automated access from this session, so no filing under ACJ was checked.
